review_object.paper: DolphinBench: Mapping the Pareto Frontier of Agent Memory

findings.assessment: Action-conditioned evaluation requires the agent to recognize that historical facts matter, then act through simulated apps. Direct QA retrieval hints are reduced but the format does not prove every implicit clue absent. Three synthetic knowledge-work personas have 200 tests each, totaling 600; 3,400–5,128 messages and roughly 500k o200k_base tokens per persona count user content only. Agents generate their own assistant replies during ingestion, so fixed user messages do not imply fixed full trajectories, tokens or costs.

The full hierarchy is persona definitions → overall narrative/quarters/weeks → app records and tool outputs → user messages → grounded facts and source alignment → task/request/check construction → finite verification/revision. Figure 1 includes source/fact links and revise/recheck. Figure 2 requires both oracle-supported runs to pass and both unsupported runs to fail. GPT-5.6-Luna receives only the original necessary messages, not an unconstrained full-history retrieval challenge. This is a selection certificate for that model and four attempts, not universal no-history impossibility, perfect full-history success, or four-run independent performance replication for each Table 2 configuration. Reading.md states these limits correctly.

Task pass is a conjunction of every required check on actual tool actions/results. GPT-5.6-Sol handles semantic equivalence from the request and checked call arguments; deterministic checks handle identifiers, values, dates, lists and tool requirements. Recipient and required content must match in the same email call; a single send cannot satisfy two distinct required emails. An acknowledgment, correct recall or success statement is insufficient. No complete semantic-judge prompt or all task-level checks are embedded in this HTML; reading.md does not claim to have read them.

All benchmark rows and partial-property footnotes were read. The three axes are action format, cost plus latency, and finite solvability certification; partial properties differ across prior benchmarks. The LoCoMo 99/1540=6.4% and approximately 63% intentionally incorrect-answer judge acceptance are attributed external audit claims, not independently reproduced findings. Reading.md preserves that distinction and does not award extra paper credit for citations.

All 13 configuration rows and all accuracy/agent-cost/memory-cost/total-cost/median-latency entries were checked against reading.md. Accuracy denominator is 600 tasks. Total dollars cover ingestion, testing and memory processing; latency is the median individual test time across personas and includes tools, not ingestion duration or a mean. Compatible integer pass totals, inferred only from rounded percentages, are Luna [394,424,411,417,355], M3 [159,287,284,246,120], Sonnet [158,194,215]. Those are arithmetic compatibility checks, not independently observed run counts. Reading.md retains the published totals despite displayed rounded component discrepancies: Luna Mem0/Honcho/Supermemory sums exceed totals by $0.01, and Sonnet Honcho sum is $0.01 below. Raw unrounded billing data were not read, so there is no verified cost-accounting defect or certified complete billing.

Luna Mem0 improves displayed accuracy by 5 percentage points and latency 44.35→37.69s at higher total cost 61.48→96.21 dollars. Luna Hindsight is 1 point higher accuracy and cheaper than Honcho but slower. Supermemory underperforms built-in for both Hermes models and costs more; for M3 it is also slower (20.00 vs 26.50%, 497.70 vs 107.03 dollars, 137.52 vs 51.40s). The highest score is 70.67%, leaving substantial errors. Memory rankings change across harness/model groups. Changes involving both model and harness cannot establish single-factor causality. No algorithm training or orthogonal component ablation is reported; comparing complete memory systems does not isolate a local retrieval-module change. No repeated-run confidence interval or broad noninferiority claim is supported.

All five limitations are present: synthetic language/style/inconsistency; only three knowledge-work domains; simulated apps without full outages or other-user edits; one to four separately scored actions rather than long workflows; and completed ingestion before testing rather than continuous interleaving. These limit direct transfer to SYSTEM-99 real-host coordination, online corrections, concurrent recovery and whole-workflow quality. The conclusion proposes future growth rather than reporting those extensions as completed.
